GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Home Depot — Q1 2026

METRIC: Comparable sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: flat to 2% growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Total-company comparable sales
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Guidance was reaffirmed after first-quarter performance was in line with expectations.
- Underlying demand was relatively similar to fiscal 2025 despite consumer uncertainty and housing-affordability pressure.

METRIC: Total sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 2.5% to 4.5% growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Total sales; reported growth
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Reflects contributions from the GMS acquisition, new stores, branches and tuck-in acquisitions.

METRIC: SRS organic sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-single-digit % organic sales growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: SRS organic sales growth
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects SRS to deliver organic growth as it expands specialty-distribution capabilities.

METRIC: New Home Depot stores
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 15 new stores
UNIT: stores
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Planned Home Depot store openings
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Part of planned investment in the business and support for the core retail network.

METRIC: New SRS locations
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 40 to 50 new SRS locations
UNIT: locations
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Planned SRS location openings
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Supports the specialty-distribution expansion strategy.

METRIC: Gross margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 33.1%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP gross margin
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The first-quarter gross-margin mix impact reflected the GMS acquisition.

METRIC: Operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 12.4% to 12.6%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP operating margin
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Full-year guidance was reaffirmed following first-quarter results in line with expectations.

METRIC: Adjusted operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 12.8% to 13.0%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Non-GAAP adjusted operating margin; excludes acquired intangible-asset amortization
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Adjusted-margin guidance excludes the expected impact of acquired intangible-asset amortization.

METRIC: Acquired intangible-asset amortization impact on adjusted operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: expected approximately 40 basis point impact
UNIT: basis points
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Impact excluded from non-GAAP adjusted operating-margin guidance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Impact relates to amortization expense from acquired intangible assets.

METRIC: Effective tax rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 24.3%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Effective tax rate
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Full-year guidance was reaffirmed.

METRIC: Net interest expense
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately $2.3 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Net interest expense
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Full-year guidance was reaffirmed.

METRIC: Diluted earnings per share growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately flat to 4.0% growth from $14.23 in fiscal 2025
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP diluted earnings per share
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Full-year guidance was reaffirmed after first-quarter performance was in line with expectations.

METRIC: Adjusted diluted earnings per share growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately flat to 4.0% growth from $14.69 in fiscal 2025
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Non-GAAP adjusted diluted earnings per share; excludes acquired intangible-asset amortization and related tax effects
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
- The adjusted measure excludes acquired intangible-asset amortization and related tax effects.

METRIC: Acquired intangible-asset amortization impact on adjusted diluted earnings per share
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: expected after-tax impact of approximately $0.50
UNIT: USD per share
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: After-tax impact excluded from non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS guidance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Impact relates to acquired intangible-asset amortization, including related tax effects.

METRIC: Capital expenditures
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately $4 billion, in line with approximately 2.5% of projected fiscal 2026 net sales
UNIT: USD billions and % of projected net sales
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Capital expenditures
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Planned investments support the strategy of driving the core and culture, building and maintaining stores, delivering a frictionless interconnected experience, and winning with Pros.

METRIC: Comparable-sales cadence
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: second half of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Half Year
BASIS: Total-company comparable sales
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects a higher comparable-sales rate in the second half solely from a return to normal storm activity.
- Management is not expecting a marked improvement in underlying demand.

METRIC: Market share
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Home-improvement market share
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects to continue growing market share through competitive advantages and ongoing investments that deliver customer experience improvements.

METRIC: Store tasking-transition completion
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: complete the transition in all stores by the end of fiscal 2026
UNIT: all stores
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: by the end of fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Transition of store tasking to the Merchandising Execution Team
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The transition is intended to create distinct selling and tasking teams, allowing Orange Apron associates to focus more on customer engagement and service.

METRIC: Share repurchases
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Capital-allocation outlook
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management has no plans to resume share repurchases during fiscal 2026.
- The company is seeking to reduce outstanding debt.
comparable_summary:
COMPARABLE EARNINGS ANALYSIS: Home Depot — Q2 2026
STRICT REPORT WINDOW: 2026-07-04 to 2026-08-16

COMPARABLE: Floor & Decor Holdings, Inc. (FND)
REPORT DATE: 2026-07-30
REPORTED PERIOD: Fiscal Q2 2026, thirteen weeks ended 2026-06-25
WHY COMPARABLE: Floor & Decor is a specialty retailer of hard-surface flooring, installation materials and related décor sold to both homeowners and professionals. It is a direct read-through for Home Depot's flooring, installation-material and large discretionary project demand, although its category concentration makes its sales trend more volatile than Home Depot's total company result.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Large discretionary home-improvement project demand
- Homeowner and professional repair-and-remodel spending
- Transaction and ticket trends in flooring and installation categories
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Uneven demand for larger discretionary home-improvement flooring projects [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Comparable store sales declined 2.1%. Management attributed the uneven demand environment to larger discretionary flooring projects, although the comparable-sales trend improved sequentially from a 5.1% decline in April to nearly flat in June. Adjusted diluted EPS was flat year over year at $0.58 and adjusted gross margin declined 20 basis points to 43.7%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative but partial read-through for Home Depot's flooring, installation and other project-based discretionary categories. Floor & Decor's concentrated flooring mix means its 2.1% comparable-sales decline should not be applied directly to Home Depot total-company comparable sales.
  SOURCE: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/FND/stock-news/99015624/form-8-k-current-report
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/FND/stock-news/99015624/form-8-k-current-report

COMPARABLE: Sherwin-Williams Company (SHW)
REPORT DATE: 2026-07-28
REPORTED PERIOD: Q2 2026, three months ended 2026-06-30
WHY COMPARABLE: Sherwin-Williams has direct exposure to U.S. paint demand, professional painters, DIY projects, paint pricing and raw-material costs. Those are shared exposures with Home Depot's paint and related project categories, though Sherwin-Williams' company-operated-store model and professional mix differ materially from Home Depot's total retail mix.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- DIY and professional paint demand
- Residential repair-and-remodel activity
- Raw-material inflation and retail pricing actions
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- No meaningful improvement in demand amid a challenging macroeconomic backdrop [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Management said there was no meaningful improvement in demand. Consolidated net sales nevertheless rose 7.5% to $6.789 billion and Paint Stores Group same-store sales rose 4.2%, but management specifically attributed sales improvement to growth investments, new-account wins and increased share of wallet; those peer-specific drivers are excluded from the Home Depot mapping.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The qualifying signal is demand stabilization rather than broad recovery. It supports a modestly cautious view of Home Depot paint and project demand, with no mechanical use of Sherwin-Williams' positive same-store-sales result.
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx
- Raw-material inflation and responsive pricing actions [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Management said pricing actions were implemented to offset raw-material inflation that pressured gross margin. The release also cited a moderate rise in raw-material costs as a partial offset to higher sales and earnings.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a mixed margin read-through: similar input-cost pressure can raise Home Depot merchandise costs, while supplier and retail pricing can offset part of that pressure. No direct Home Depot gross-margin or EPS percentage is inferred because pass-through, category mix and merchant terms differ.
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx

COMPARABLE: SiteOne Landscape Supply, Inc. (SITE)
REPORT DATE: 2026-07-29
REPORTED PERIOD: Q2 2026, three months ended 2026-06-28
WHY COMPARABLE: SiteOne supplies residential and commercial landscape professionals. It is a direct category and professional-demand read-through for Home Depot's outdoor, lawn-and-garden, hardscape and repair-and-upgrade activity, though SiteOne is a wholesale distributor and therefore has a substantially more professional and outdoor-concentrated customer base.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Residential repair-and-upgrade activity
- New residential construction and outdoor-project demand
- Landscape-product pricing, freight and distribution costs
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Softer new-residential-construction and repair-and-upgrade end markets [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Organic Daily Sales increased 1%, with price inflation and commercial initiatives partly offsetting softer demand in new residential construction and repair-and-upgrade end markets. Management estimated new residential construction was down high single digits and repair-and-upgrade was down mid single digits. Net sales increased 5.0% to $1.531 billion, including $49.2 million from acquisitions, so acquisitions are excluded from the read-through.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The mid-single-digit repair-and-upgrade weakness is a negative read-through for Home Depot's outdoor project, landscape and related repair categories. It is scaled down heavily because Home Depot has a much broader assortment and a larger DIY mix.
  SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228
- Price inflation responding to higher costs, partly offset by freight and distribution costs [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Pricing was up 3% in the quarter. Gross margin expanded 50 basis points to 36.9%, primarily from higher price realization and commercial initiatives, partially offset by higher freight and distribution costs and commodity deflation in certain products.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The result supports a mixed Home Depot margin signal: price realization can cushion cost pressure, but freight and distribution inflation can limit the benefit. The add-on does not credit SiteOne's commercial initiatives or acquisition contribution to Home Depot.
  SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228

PRELIMINARY COMPARABLE-ONLY METRIC ADD-ONS:
- Net sales: -226 USDm (DECREASE)
  CALCULATION: Comparable-sales add-on = [FND comparable sales decline of -2.1% × 15% transmission weight] + [SiteOne repair-and-upgrade demand decline of -5.0%, using the midpoint of 'mid single digits,' × 4% transmission weight] + [Sherwin-Williams qualitative demand signal × 0] = -0.315pp - 0.200pp + 0.000pp = -0.515pp, rounded to -0.5pp. Dollar conversion = -0.5% × USD45,277m illustrative Home Depot Q2 sales scaling base = -USD226.4m, rounded to -USD226m.
  ASSUMPTION: The 15% Floor & Decor transmission weight is deliberately partial because flooring and large discretionary projects are important but not representative of Home Depot's total basket.
  ASSUMPTION: The 4% SiteOne transmission weight reflects a narrower outdoor/landscape and professional-project exposure within Home Depot's broader mix.
  ASSUMPTION: Sherwin-Williams contributes no quantified sales point because its reported sales growth was expressly driven by peer-specific investments, account wins and share-of-wallet gains; only its qualitative lack-of-demand-recovery observation is retained.
  ASSUMPTION: The USD45,277m scaling base is used solely to express the comparable-sales signal in the requested USDm unit; this is an incremental add-on rather than an absolute Home Depot sales forecast.
  ASSUMPTION: The peer fiscal-quarter ends of June 25, June 28 and June 30 are treated as sufficiently aligned with the intended Home Depot Q2 read-through period.
  SOURCE: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/FND/stock-news/99015624/form-8-k-current-report
  SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx
- Adjusted diluted EPS: -0.02 USD / share (DECREASE)
  CALCULATION: EPS add-on converts the -USD226m sales signal using a 10% assumed incremental after-tax earnings conversion and 994m assumed diluted shares: -USD226m × 10% / 994m = -USD0.0227 per share, rounded to -USD0.02 per share. No positive EPS credit is taken for peer tariff refunds, acquisition effects, share repurchases, commercial initiatives, new-account wins or other peer-specific execution.
  ASSUMPTION: A 10% after-tax incremental conversion is a conservative modeling assumption for an incremental sales signal, not an assertion of Home Depot's reported margin.
  ASSUMPTION: The 994m diluted-share denominator is a unit-conversion assumption only.
  ASSUMPTION: Sherwin-Williams' raw-material inflation and SiteOne's freight and distribution costs support retaining the full negative sales-to-EPS conversion rather than assuming margin expansion.
  ASSUMPTION: Floor & Decor's tariff-refund effect and Masco's tariff-refund benefit are excluded as non-comparable items.
  SOURCE: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/FND/stock-news/99015624/form-8-k-current-report
  SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx
- Comparable sales, total company: -0.5 % (DECREASE)
  CALCULATION: Central comparable-only add-on = [Floor & Decor -2.1% comparable-store sales × 15% transmission weight] + [SiteOne -5.0% repair-and-upgrade demand proxy × 4% transmission weight] = -0.515 percentage points, rounded to -0.5 percentage points. Sherwin-Williams is assigned a zero numerical contribution because its release quantified no broad demand recovery but reported positive sales results driven by excluded company-specific share gains.
  ASSUMPTION: Percent values are percentage-point add-ons, not percentage changes.
  ASSUMPTION: SiteOne's 'mid single digits' repair-and-upgrade decline is represented by -5.0% for central-value calculation.
  ASSUMPTION: Transmission weights are exposure adjustments, not estimates of Home Depot category sales mix and not copied peer percentage changes.
  ASSUMPTION: The result is a preliminary incremental signal only; it does not incorporate target-company news, analyst estimates, stock-price reactions, results released after 2026-08-16 or non-qualifying peers.
  SOURCE: https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/NYSE/FND/stock-news/99015624/form-8-k-current-report
  SOURCE: https://investors.siteone.com/news-releases/2026/07-29-2026-110035228
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-Second-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx

events.title: Lowe's first-quarter 2026 results and affirmed outlook
events.summary: Lowe's reported first-quarter sales of $23.1 billion and comparable-sales growth of 0.6%. It cited spring execution, 15.5% online-sales growth, and strength in appliances, home services and Pro sales, and reaffirmed its fiscal-2026 outlook.
source_headlines: Lowe’s reports first-quarter 2026 sales and earnings; affirms full-year outlook

events.title: Home Depot declares quarterly cash dividend
events.summary: Home Depot declared a quarterly cash dividend of $2.33 per share. The dividend was payable on June 18, 2026, to shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.
source_headlines: The Home Depot declares quarterly dividend of $2.33 per share

events.title: May U.S. existing-home sales increase
events.summary: U.S. existing-home sales rose 3.2% month over month in May to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.17 million, the highest pace since December. Sales also rose year over year, while higher mortgage rates and tight inventory remained constraints.
source_headlines: U.S. existing-home sales rise 3.2% in May despite higher mortgage rates

events.title: Federal Reserve holds policy rate at June meeting
events.summary: The Federal Reserve left the federal-funds target range unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75% on June 17, 2026. Meeting materials and contemporaneous coverage indicated that policymakers remained focused on inflation and that policy could remain restrictive.
source_headlines: Federal Reserve holds policy rate at 3.50%-3.75% at June meeting

events.title: Home Depot expands Pro Xtra Rewards partner offers
events.summary: Home Depot added Pro Xtra partner offers from 7-Eleven, Jimmy John's, Tecovas, and Rosie's AI Answering Service. The company said the benefits are available to all members and refresh quarterly, and that two-thirds of Pro online users regularly use its app.
source_headlines: The Home Depot expands Pro Xtra Rewards with third-party business and lifestyle offers

events.title: Home Depot launches APO/FPO delivery through military exchanges
events.summary: Home Depot launched APO/FPO delivery through partnerships with the Army & Air Force Exchange Service and Navy Exchange. The program covers more than 20,000 products, more than 750 overseas bases in over 80 countries, and more than 250,000 overseas military families.
source_headlines: The Home Depot launches APO/FPO delivery through military exchanges

events.title: June U.S. existing-home sales decline
events.summary: U.S. existing-home sales fell 2.4% in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.09 million. The report cited record home prices and elevated mortgage rates as affordability constraints.
source_headlines: U.S. existing-home sales fall 2.4% in June as prices reach a record and mortgage rates remain elevated

events.title: June U.S. single-family housing starts and permits decline
events.summary: June single-family housing starts fell 0.2% to an annualized rate of 895,000, while single-family permits fell 2.4% to 871,000. The reported factors included higher mortgage rates and inventory of unsold new homes.
source_headlines: U.S. single-family starts and permits fall in June

events.title: United States imposes new tariffs on imports from 60 trading partners
events.summary: The United States imposed 10% and 12.5% Section 301 tariffs on goods from 60 trading partners as a temporary 10% global tariff expired. The duties reportedly covered 99.4% of U.S. imports, subject to listed exemptions.
source_headlines: U.S. imposes new 10% and 12.5% tariffs on imports from 60 trading partners

events.title: June U.S. new-home sales increase but remain below prior year
events.summary: June new single-family home sales rose 1.6% month over month to an annualized rate of 628,000, but were 5.6% below the prior-year level. Higher mortgage rates and affordability were reported as continuing constraints.
source_headlines: U.S. new-home sales rise in June, but remain constrained by mortgage rates and affordability

events.title: Federal Reserve holds policy rate at July meeting
events.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained the federal-funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75% on July 29, 2026. Its statement said inflation remained elevated in part because supply shocks had increased prices in certain sectors, including energy; three policymakers preferred a quarter-point increase.
source_headlines: Federal Reserve holds policy rate at 3.50%-3.75% in July amid elevated inflation and energy supply shocks

events.title: Home Depot announces organizational realignment
events.summary: Home Depot announced a leadership and organizational realignment intended to improve customer experience, accelerate innovation, and capture market share. The company unified private-brand and core merchandising; integrated customer experience, online, financial-services, and loyalty functions; and created an Office of Pro Acceleration to coordinate Home Depot Pro, HD Supply, SRS, and Construction Resources, including shared CRM, product-catalog, and fulfillment capabilities.
source_headlines: The Home Depot announces organizational realignment focused on merchandising, loyalty, finance, Pro and technology

events.title: July U.S. retail sales decline while building-material and garden merchants gain
events.summary: U.S. retail sales fell 0.6% in July. Building-material and garden-supply merchants were among the categories that posted sales gains.
source_headlines: U.S. retail sales fall in July, while building-material and garden-supply merchants post gains

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Forecast Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales = $47,088m; previous reported Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales = $41,765m; projected change = $47,088m - $41,765m = +$5,323m. FY guidance midpoint is 3.5% total-sales growth: fiscal 2025 sales of $164,700m × 1.035 = $170,465m. Q2 is phased at $47,088m, reflecting Q2's historically larger seasonal sales base, a roughly 0.5% core comparable-sales assumption, annualized GMS contribution that was only partly present in Q2 fiscal 2025, and new stores/branches. Reconciliation: Q1 actual $41,765m + Q2 forecast $47,088m = H1 $88,853m; implied H2 sales = FY midpoint $170,465m - H1 $88,853m = $81,612m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, selling price, acquisition mix and new-store/branch sales
event_contributions.transmission_path: Core comparable sales plus GMS annualization, new stores and SRS branches flow into net sales; net sales is the reported consolidated revenue metric.
assumptions: Uses the midpoint of management's FY total-sales-growth range: 3.5%.
Q2 fiscal 2025 sales were $45,277m; Q2 fiscal 2026 includes a full-quarter GMS contribution versus no GMS ownership in the prior-year Q2.

Core Q2 comparable-sales assumption is approximately +0.5%, consistent with Q1's +0.6%, management's statement that no marked underlying-demand improvement is expected, and higher storm-driven comp expected only in H2.
The $47,088m Q2 estimate leaves FY midpoint arithmetic intact; it is not an FY figure mechanically divided by four.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. FY midpoint sales = $164,700m × (1 + 3.5%) = $170,465m. Q2 phase = prior-year Q2 $45,277m + approximately $226m from 0.5% core comparable growth + approximately $1,300m annualized GMS timing/mix + approximately $285m new stores, branches and tuck-ins = $47,088m. Contribution versus previous Q1 actual = $47,088m - $41,765m = +$5,323m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume and Pro-category mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lowe's spring execution and positive comparable sales could corroborate sector demand; however, no separate Home Depot revenue adjustment is supportable after management had already reaffirmed its FY range using contemporaneous market information.
assumptions: Lowe's 0.6% comparable-sales result is a broad industry corroboration, not a Home Depot category-level sales measure.
Avoids double counting the same spring demand conditions embedded in GUIDANCE.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Incremental Home Depot Q2 sales effect = $0m because the peer result broadly confirms, rather than changes, the management-guided demand baseline.

event_contributions.affected_line: Financing cash flow and retained earnings
event_contributions.transmission_path: Cash dividend payment reduces cash and equity but does not change revenue recognition or Q2 net sales.
assumptions: No change to store activity, customer demand or selling price is disclosed.
event_contributions.calculation: DISCRETE/TIMED ROUTE. Net-sales effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Housing turnover and project-sales volume
event_contributions.transmission_path: Higher May existing-home sales can support repair-and-remodel activity and therefore sales volume, but the one-month move is within the housing-affordability and uncertain-demand environment already contemplated in guidance.
assumptions: No Home Depot-specific conversion rate from monthly existing-home sales to Q2 sales is disclosed.
June housing data subsequently reversed part of the May improvement; no standalone add-on is used.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 net-sales effect = $0m; the May macro signal is treated as already within GUIDANCE and is not separately monetized.

event_contributions.affected_line: Housing affordability and project-sales volume
event_contributions.transmission_path: Restrictive policy rates can suppress turnover and larger project initiation, reducing sales volume; management already cited housing-affordability pressure and retained its FY sales range.
assumptions: No same-quarter change in Home Depot customer demand can be isolated from the June FOMC decision.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 net-sales effect = $0m because the rates-and-affordability risk was already contemplated by GUIDANCE.

event_contributions.affected_line: Pro loyalty, customer frequency and promotional expense
event_contributions.transmission_path: Additional Pro Xtra partner offers could increase engagement and future sales frequency, but no enrollment, spend, cost or Q2 realization amount is disclosed.
assumptions: Quarterly partner-offer refresh implies an early-stage, unquantified program rather than a measurable Q2 sales event.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 net-sales effect = $0m because no defensible revenue conversion is available.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume and fulfillment capacity
event_contributions.transmission_path: APO/FPO delivery expands addressable demand but may also create fulfillment costs; no launch-period order volume or revenue conversion is disclosed.
assumptions: The July launch is too late and too small relative to consolidated sales to quantify reliably within Q2.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Incremental Q2 net-sales effect = $0m.

event_contributions.affected_line: Housing turnover and larger-project sales volume
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower June existing-home sales can pressure project demand and sales volume, but it offsets the preceding May improvement and remains consistent with the affordability pressures already embedded in guidance.
assumptions: No defensible monthly housing-sales-to-Home-Depot-sales elasticity is provided.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Forecast Q2 fiscal 2026 adjusted diluted EPS = $4.7919, rounded to $4.79; previous reported Q1 fiscal 2026 adjusted diluted EPS = $3.43; projected change = $4.7919 - $3.43 = +$1.3619, rounded to +$1.36. The bridge uses adjusted operating margin, since adjusted EPS excludes acquired-intangible amortization and related tax effects.

event_contributions.affected_line: Sales volume, gross margin/mix, operating expenses, interest expense and tax
event_contributions.transmission_path: Q2 net sales of $47,088m × phased adjusted operating margin of 14.6% = adjusted operating income; less Q2 interest expense, then tax, produces adjusted net income; divided by diluted shares produces adjusted diluted EPS.
assumptions: The FY adjusted-operating-margin midpoint is 12.9%, but Q2 is not assigned the FY rate directly: Q2 historically has a seasonally higher margin.
Q2 adjusted operating margin is phased at 14.6%, 20 basis points below fiscal 2025 Q2's 14.8% adjusted margin, reflecting GMS mix and continued cost/price uncertainty.
Q2 net interest expense is phased at $570m, close to the prior-year Q2 seasonal amount and consistent with FY guidance of approximately $2.3bn.
Tax rate is 24.3% per guidance; diluted shares are 996m, equal to Q1 reported diluted weighted-average shares because repurchases remain paused.

Annual reconciliation: FY adjusted operating income = $170,465m × 12.9% = $21,990m. Q1 actual adjusted operating income was $5,152m and Q2 forecast is $6,875m, leaving $9,963m for H2 on $81,612m of implied H2 sales, or 12.2%, consistent with lower H2 seasonal margin.
event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Q2 adjusted operating income = $47,088m × 14.6% = $6,874.848m. Pretax adjusted income = $6,874.848m - $570m + $0m = $6,304.848m. Adjusted net income = $6,304.848m × (1 - 24.3%) + $0m = $4,772.770m. Adjusted diluted EPS = $4,772.770m / 996m shares × 1 = $4.7919. Contribution versus Q1 actual adjusted EPS = $4.7919 - $3.43 = +$1.3619, rounded to +$1.36.

event_contributions.calculation: Incremental adjusted operating income = $0m; EPS effect = $0m × (1 - 24.3%) / 996m = $0.00.

earnings_bridge.calculation: Adjusted operating income = revenue × adjusted operating margin + other operating income = $47,088m × 14.6% + $0m = $6,874.848m. Pretax adjusted income = $6,874.848m - $570m + $0m = $6,304.848m. Adjusted net income = $6,304.848m × (1 - 24.3%) + $0m = $4,772.770m. Adjusted diluted EPS = $4,772.770m / 996m shares × 1 = $4.7919, or $4.79. The margin is phased from the FY 12.9% adjusted operating-margin midpoint using Q2's historical seasonality rather than applying the annual rate directly to Q2.
assumptions: All dollar income-statement inputs and diluted shares are in millions.
The 14.6% Q2 adjusted operating margin excludes acquired-intangible amortization, matching the requested adjusted EPS basis.
No incremental event contribution is included unless separately quantifiable and not already incorporated in guidance.
No share repurchases are assumed, consistent with management's stated fiscal-2026 plan.

event_contributions.calculation: ANNUAL/RUN-RATE ROUTE. Q2 total-company comp forecast = +0.5%. Sequential contribution relative to Q1 reported +0.6% = +0.5% - +0.6% = -0.1 percentage points.
